- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 10d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7d horizon.
- If official supply net is strongly bearish (net < -20) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.33/1.00 alternation), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5d average if sentiment shifts.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and net supply negative, model tends to overreact to recent auction events; dampen forecast growth by 5–10% if last 3 events are supply-driven.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and true outcome is rising, model underestimates momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% if recent 10d mean is rising and sentiment is weak.
- When sentiment is high but true outcome is flat or declining, model overestimates bullishness; reduce forecast by 3–7% if sentiment >0.67 and price action contradicts sentiment.
